source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Draw a graph showing the emissions reported and determine if the numbers reported in any of the reports are more than 3 standard deviations away from average. If the pollution levels are higher than 3 standard deviations, note the report date.
3. Search the local newspaper for reports of "upsets" or "malfunctions" that match the report date identified in Step 2.
4. Write a detailed report and note that any of the emissions numbers that are more than 3 standard deviations away from average may be due to an "upset" or "malfunction".

For example, in the report for the Flint Hills Resources refinery in Pine Bend, Minnesota, the monitoring records show that the Nitrogen Oxides (NOx) emissions reported for January 2009 were more than 3 standard deviations away from average.
